findings.text: §7's done-when states a hard threshold (every `/_index` answers 200 in under 1 s in both passes, the port accepts within 5 s) but names no negative control, unlike every other node in this plan, so nothing in the node shows the gate can fail

findings.reason: the node cannot be closed on one verdict; the plan should split §10 or declare a control per deliverable.
findings.text: §10's three deliverable bullets are three separately-gated behaviours across three source files, and its single declared negative control ("restores the wholesale replacement of `window.STATE` on revalidation") falsifies only the first, so the stale-schedule behaviour and the re-render behaviour would be closed on a gate that proves neither

findings.reason: §8 is landed and the premise stands; the correction is a citation edit to a done section, not a change to work a later node does.
findings.text: §8 cites the MCP/CLI `discover_plans` callers as `reckon/mcp.py` line 1250 and `reckon/mcp_views.py` line 1985; at `8945ecb16` line 1250 is a `return data, version` and line 1985 is a resource-model branch, and the plan's own comment correction (`reckon/mcp.py:1646`, `reckon/mcp_views.py:2454-2458`) lands on a row-building `except` clause and `_followup_record` respectively, so no citation in the plan leads a reader to the caller it names

findings.reason: as written the change would leave the crew view's derived flow — the very surface §10 exists to keep on screen — stale between the project's own document changes, which §11's request-count measure would score as success.
findings.text: §11's premise, that a fleet event costs an `/_index` and `/_discover` pair "for a page whose own payloads have not changed", is false for the payload's schedule: `_attach_schedule_for_read` builds it from live crew rows (`schedule_report(project, inventory, _crew_rows(mounts, project), ...)`, `reckon/serve.py:1765-1772`) and attaches it per request rather than caching it, so the schedule changes whenever crew runs change, while the fleet-scoped rollup is the only wake those changes reach the page through; §11's fix removes the loader's only refresh path for it (crew.jsx reads `window.STATE.schedule`, and no view-level `reckon-fleet` listener carries the schedule)

findings.reason: deliverable 3's stated contrast ("re-renders when the derived merge lands, not at the next crew poll") rests on that claim, so a builder following it cannot tell whether the merge already re-renders and may add a second render path (or skip the work as already satisfied).
findings.text: §10's fourth cause ("Nothing re-renders on that [the derived merge]") is contradicted by the cited file: `refreshProjectState` calls `loadChecksAfterDerived`, which awaits `window.STATE_DERIVED_READY` and then `loadDocumentChecks`, whose success path dispatches `reckon:checks` (`docs/ui/state-loader.js:253`), an event `shell.jsx:168` answers with `bumpInv`, so a render does follow the merge after one `/_checks` round trip
